justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Systematic reviews show small positive effects on balance and motor function; effect sizes modest vs dose-matched alternatives.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: PATH International certification; equine-assisted therapy requires horse facility access; significant logistics.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Extremely limited by requirement for horse facility and trained animal; applicable only in equine therapy settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Very limited coverage; PATH certification required by the few payers that cover; mostly self-pay or disability grants.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Very limited employer demand; primarily nonprofit equine therapy centers and adaptive sports programs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Exceptional; children and adults with disabilities report transformative experience. Motivation to attend is unmatched.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Families of pediatric clients with disabilities frequently pay cash or use grants when insurance won't cover equine-assisted therapy.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Scarcity and experiential value support premium per-session pricing, though overhead eats much of the margin.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Highly distinctive; very few clinicians offer it in any given region, creating a near-monopoly niche.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Hard to scale: requires horses, land, certified clinicians, and PATH-credentialed staff; labor and capital intensive.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Parents in special-needs communities actively seek it out, but absolute demand volume is small.
justifications.business.efficiency: Expensive and slow to implement; facility, livestock, and credentialing costs are substantial relative to revenue.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Niche modality with minimal weight in faculty promotion or hiring outside a few specialized programs.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Some peer-reviewed work exists but the field is small and methodologically limited.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Tangential to core PT/OT curricula; appears at most as a brief elective topic.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence is growing but consists largely of small studies; RCTs are limited and heterogeneous.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Virtually never listed as a desired credential in faculty job postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Substantial time and money to credential with little return in academic currency.
